items.title: Section: Virtues Three Through Ten, and Moral Discipline Closes at the Fascicle's True End

items.zh: 復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，遍諸方域，妙善稱譽聲頌普聞。是名第三尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，寢安、覺安，遠離一切身心熱惱。是名第四尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，若寢、若覺，諸天保護。是名第五尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，於他凶暴不慮其惡，無諸怖畏，心離驚恐。是名第六尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅。諸憙殺者、怨讎惡友，雖得其隙，亦常保護，了知此是具戒士夫補特伽羅，或為善友，或住中平。是名第七尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，一切魍魎、藥叉、宅神、非人之類，雖得其便、雖得其隙，而常保護。謂具尸羅增上力故。是名第八尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，法無艱難，從他獲得種種利養。所謂衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥及諸資具。由依尸羅增上因力，國王、大臣，及諸黎庶、饒財長者，及商主等恭敬尊重。是名第九尸羅律儀功德勝利。復有所餘具戒士夫補特伽羅，一切所願皆得稱遂。若於欲界，願樂當生或剎帝利大族姓家、或婆羅門大族姓家、或諸居士大族姓家、或諸長者大族姓家、或四大王眾天、或三十三天、或夜摩天、或覩史多天、或化樂天、或他化自在天眾同分中，由戒淨故，即隨所願當得往生。若復願樂入諸靜慮現法樂住，或有色天眾同分中若住、若生，由戒淨故，便得離欲，所願皆遂。若復願樂寂靜勝解，超過色定，入無色定具足安住，或無色天眾同分中當得往生，餘如前說。若復願樂當證最極究竟涅槃，由戒淨故，便證一切究竟離欲。是名第十尸羅律儀功德勝利。如是已說戒蘊廣辨、戒蘊虧損、戒蘊圓滿、戒蘊異門、戒蘊觀察及以清淨、戒蘊所有功德勝利。於此宣說明了開示一切種相，最極圓滿資糧所攝尸羅律儀。若有自愛樂沙門性、婆羅門性諸善男子，應勤修學。
items.en: There is, further, a person possessing discipline whose excellent reputation and praise spread and are heard throughout every region … who sleeps in peace and wakes in peace, free of all bodily and mental distress … who, whether sleeping or waking, is protected by the gods … who, before the violent, feels no concern for their malice, no fear at all, the mind free of alarm … whom even those who delight in killing, enemies and ill-wishers, though given the opportunity, nonetheless protect … whom even every kind of spirit, yakṣa, house-deity, and nonhuman being, though given the opportunity, nonetheless constantly protects … who, invariably and without hardship, receives offerings of every kind from others … all of whose wishes are fulfilled … and who, wishing to realise the utmost, final nirvāṇa, thereby realises complete and final freedom from desire, because of discipline's purity. This is the tenth excellent virtue of moral restraint. …Here it has been clearly taught and revealed, in every one of its aspects, the moral restraint comprised within the most perfectly complete provisions for the path. Whatever good sons genuinely delight in the recluse's nature, the brahmin's nature, should diligently train in this.

blocks.text: A short day to close fascicle 22 and the long section on moral discipline.

One of pure discipline: has a good name heard everywhere; sleeps and wakes in peace; is protected by gods; has no fear of the violent; is cared for even by enemies; is not troubled by spirits; dies without regret; is reborn in heaven; finds no hardship; and has every wish fulfilled. Venerable Miào Jìng: 法 in "法無艱難" means "constantly", that is, such a person constantly lives without hardship.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "having formed no bad ties with others, there is nothing to fear." "Abiding" in the realm of concentration and "being born" there both rest on discipline kept in the desire realm.
The section ends: whoever loves themselves should keep pure discipline. Master Cháng Bǎi: people pursuing fame and wealth do not truly love themselves; a practitioner seeking the good does.

Moral discipline has been examined from every side: its six aspects, three marks and natures, ten impairments, six names, three observations, ten benefits. The next fascicle turns to the remaining provisions: sense restraint, moderation in eating, and wakefulness.

quiz.q: In his outline, how does Master Cháng Bǎi classify the first and second virtues?
options: first is higher rebirth, second decisive excellence
the first is the benefit of decisive excellence; the second, of higher rebirth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first virtue explains the benefit of attaining decisive excellence; the second explains the benefit of higher rebirth. The first leads to liberation and nirvāṇa; the second is dying without regret and going to a good destiny.

quiz.q: The disciplined are said to "die well, pass away early well." How can early death be good, per the masters?
options: what matters is whether this life's conduct was good; with pure conduct, departing at any time is auspicious
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: dying early is not necessarily bad; what matters is whether one's bodily, verbal, and mental deeds in this life were good or evil. Venerable Miào Jìng: as long as your body, speech, and mind are pure while you live, whenever you go is fine — it is auspicious.

quiz.q: What do the third through tenth virtues include?
options: renown; peaceful sleep and waking; divine protection; fearlessness before the violent; protection by enemies; protection by nonhumans; receiving offerings without hardship; every wish fulfilled, up to final dispassion
quiz.why: The treatise lists: renown heard everywhere; peaceful sleep and waking; protection by gods; no fear of the violent; protection even by killers and enemies; protection by nonhumans; offerings received without hardship; all wishes fulfilled. Master Cháng Bǎi: even enemies will protect such a person.

quiz.q: The ninth virtue "法無艱難" is rendered "the path is without hardship." How does Venerable Miào Jìng gloss 法?
options: 法 means "constantly" — the pure-precepted person is constantly without hardship
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: in "法無艱難," 法 means "constant" — the person of pure discipline has no hardship. The English "path" differs.

quiz.q: The sixth virtue, "no fear before the violent" — what reason do the masters give?
options: Cháng Bǎi: having made no bad karmic ties, there is nothing to fear; Miào Jìng: gods protect him, so none can harm him
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: since he has formed no bad ties with others and created no such evil karma, there is nothing to fear. Venerable Miào Jìng: since the gods protect him, nothing happens — no one can harm him.

quiz.q: The tenth virtue includes wishes for the form realm. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "若住、若生"?
options: "abiding" is attaining form-realm concentration while in the desire realm; "being born" is being reborn in the form heavens after death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "abiding" means keeping pure discipline in the desire realm and attaining form-realm concentration; "being born" means attaining it and, after death, being reborn in the form heavens. This requires meditation, but pure discipline gives the capacity to fulfil the wish.

quiz.q: The fascicle closes urging "good sons who delight in the recluse's nature" to train. How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain this self-love?
options: chasing fame and wealth is not true self-love; seeking the good is
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinary people pursuing fame, gain, and worldly wealth do not truly love themselves; a practitioner seeking the good does. The most perfect completion is the goal; the provisions are the means to nirvāṇa.
